items.title: Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen
items.blurb: We find that frontier LLMs are surprisingly good at natively reading and writing neural network weights, well past what we’d expect from humans or conventional algorithms.

items.title: The 'Astra can read and write weights to improve Qwen' post is misleading
items.blurb: The experiments that read raw weights and the ones that fix Qwen use completely different techniques.

items.title: A Decade of Kill Bugs – Alan Grow
items.blurb: … A bug in kill was so surprising that, once I'd found it, I couldn't stop there. I needed to know how this bug came to be, and what had led the programmers so badly astray.

items.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996?
items.blurb: A fun experiment where I back-port all the improvements we've made to chess engines over the last 30 years and run it on a 1996 Pentium Pro to see what we could have done if only we knew more at the time.

items.title: Nvidia – open-source auto-ontology
items.blurb: Auto Ontology is a Python framework for building semantic, graph-based reasoning layers over data. It enables deterministic query generation, better context retrieval, and more explainable AI for LLM and agent workflows.

items.title: Show HN: Hacker Times, a New York Times-inspired version of Hacker News

items.title: Designing a planned switchover for minimum disruption
items.blurb: How Neki uses preflight checks, query buffering, synchronous replication, and fast rollback to make Postgres primary switchovers less disruptive.
